newsitem.title: USA: DC panel orders city to overhaul FY 98 budget plan.
newsitem.headline: DC panel orders city to overhaul FY 98 budget plan.

text.p: The District of Columbia's financial control board informally rejected city Mayor Marion Barry's proposed fiscal 1998 budget on Wednesday and ordered him to overhaul the plan by February 28, the board announced.

The panel said Barry's plan is incomplete and does not "promote financial stability" as required by the 1995 federal law that created the five-member control board and ordered the city to balance its budget by fiscal 1999.

The panel, chaired by economist Andrew Brimmer, said in a press statement it opposes a Barry plan to restructure $50 million of the city's long-term debt in fiscal 1998. The plan would cost the city more than it would save over the full term of the bonds, the panel said.
The board also said Barry's plan does not account for certain types of funds, including grants and "intra-District" funds.
While Barry's plan purportedly balances D.C.'s budget in fiscal 1998, it would leave the city's fiscal 1999 budget unbalanced, the control board said.
The city's deficit also would increase substantially in fiscal years 2000 and 2001 under Barry's plan, the panel added.
The board cancelled a public meeting set for 1400 EST today where it was set to take a formal vote on Barry's budget.
